resources.string: Progress while a document is being sent to a printer
Printing from Android to a Bluetooth thermal printer, without a cloud service, an account, or a PC in the middle. Everything happens on this device and your own network.
Bluetooth, when you set up a printer

To send the printer its job, and nothing else. Finding it is done by Android\'s own device picker, which scans on PocketPrint\'s behalf — so this app never scans, and never asks for a location permission on any version of Android.
A print job runs in the background so that leaving the app does not kill the transfer. The notification is how you see progress and how you cancel a job that has gone wrong.
No account, no analytics, no network calls except to your own printer. Documents are read through Android\'s file picker, so PocketPrint never asks for access to your storage or your photos.
Nothing is requested yet. Each permission is asked for at the moment it is needed, and the app keeps working without them - it just cannot do the part that needs them.
The first page, exactly as it will be sent: one bit per dot, at the printer\'s own head width and resolution.

Word, Excel and PowerPoint files cannot be laid out on the phone without a full office engine. Point this at a converter that accepts a multipart upload and returns a PDF - a Gotenberg instance on your LAN works as-is. Leave it blank to disable.
Turning this on lets any app print to your saved printers, including Bluetooth ones, through the standard Android print dialog.
Set up a label or receipt printer
Pairs, connects, asks the printer which command language it speaks, configures the label size, prints a test label, and adds it to Android\'s print dialog.
Label stock loaded in the printer
This has to match the labels actually loaded. Set it too long and the printer feeds forward looking for a gap that is not there, then stops with a paper fault.
No paired Bluetooth printers found. Pair the printer in Android Settings first — the PIN is usually 0000 — then come back and try again.
The printer cannot answer this one. Whatever happened, it reports paper loaded, head down and no error.
It printed, but the output is wrong
This printer is now marked as confirmed by an actual label. That is the only confirmation Bluetooth and USB can give — neither protocol reports what the printer did with the bytes.
That is almost always the paper.

Thermal printers have no ink: they mark heat-sensitive stock, on one side only. Ordinary paper labels, or a thermal roll loaded upside down, feed perfectly and stay white. Check the stock, then print another test from the printer\'s settings.
The printer is not listening in the dialect it was sent, so it is printing the commands instead of obeying them.
Change it in the printer\'s settings, where there is a test-page button.
If the printer spits out pages of readable commands instead of your label, this is the setting that is wrong.

How the printer finds the top of the next label. Set to look for a gap that is not there, it feeds forward hunting for one and stops with a paper fault. Nothing in the protocol can tell you which is right, which is why it is a setting.
The most common adjustment there is. Too light and barcodes scan intermittently or not at all; too dark and thin bars bleed together and also stop scanning.
Feeds a few labels while the printer works out where the gaps are. Worth doing when printing drifts onto the join between two labels.
203 dpi heads: 384 for 58 mm, 576 for 80 mm, 812 for 4 inch.
Send test page with these settings
No label or receipt printers saved yet. Pair one over Bluetooth, then save it on the Print tab.

The barcode is always generated by the printer\'s own firmware rather than sent as an image, which lands the bars on exact dot boundaries and keeps them scannable at small sizes.\n\nText uses the printer\'s built-in fonts when it can. Those fonts hold Latin characters and nothing else, so anything they cannot carry - Hindi, Arabic, Thai, Chinese - is laid out on the phone and sent as an image instead. That takes a little longer over Bluetooth and prints correctly, rather than being fast and full of question marks.

Android will switch PocketPrint off if it is not opened for about three months, and take its Bluetooth permission with it. Printing from other apps does not count as opening it - so the next print from Gmail would simply fail, inside Gmail, with nothing able to explain why. Turning off \"pause app activity if unused\" prevents it.
PocketPrint cannot see or reach Bluetooth printers, because the Bluetooth permission was turned down. Android will not ask again, so it has to be granted in app settings.
No saved printers yet. Scan below, or add one by IP address.
Nothing found yet. Wi-Fi printers must be on the same network; Bluetooth printers must already be paired in Android Settings.
PocketPrint is switched on as a print service. Saved printers appear in every app\'s print dialog, including Bluetooth ones.
PocketPrint is not switched on as a print service, so it will not appear in other apps\' print dialogs. Turn it on under Settings > Connected devices > Printing.

To print from other apps, turn PocketPrint on under Settings > Connected devices > Printing. Saved printers appear in every app\'s print dialog, including Bluetooth ones. This version of Android will not tell PocketPrint whether the switch is already on.
The printer closed the connection part way through. Thermal printers sleep aggressively - wake it and try again.
The printer stopped taking bytes without closing the connection, which usually means it is out of paper, its cover is open, or it is waiting at a fault it has not reported.
Turn Bluetooth on and try again.
PocketPrint needs the Bluetooth permission to reach this printer. Grant it in Android\'s app settings.
The printer answered but is not listening on that port. Check the port number - raw printing is usually 9100, IPP is 631.
The printer did not answer. Check it is switched on, and that it is in range or on the same network.
That address cannot be reached from this network. A printer on a different subnet, or a phone on mobile data rather than Wi-Fi, will both look like this.
Something else is already connected to this printer. These printers accept one connection at a time.
Pairing failed. Remove the printer in Android\'s Bluetooth settings and pair it again - the PIN is usually 0000.
That printer is no longer saved. Set it up again.
The printer reports it is out of media.
Bluetooth printing carries no acknowledgement. The printer accepted the bytes; only the label tells you what it did with them.
USB printing carries no acknowledgement. The printer accepted the bytes; only the page tells you what it did with them.
Raw port 9100 carries no acknowledgement. The printer accepted the bytes; only the page tells you what it did with them.
The printer accepted the job but never said what became of it.
The printer accepted the job but gave it no id, so its progress cannot be followed.
The printer stopped answering questions about job %1$d, so what became of it is unknown.
The printer no longer has a record of job %1$d. That usually means it finished, but the printer never said so.
The printer refused to report on job %1$d (%2$s).
The printer was still %1$s after %2$s, so it was left to get on with it.
Waiting for another job on %1$s to finish
Android stopped this job because it ran too long.
Could not read the document from the print system
That printer is no longer saved in PocketPrint
Ask the printer what it speaks
Work out label size and head width
No reply, so %1$s assumed from the name
Now offered in every app\'s print dialog
%1$s has no media sensor to calibrate.
%1$s is no longer saved, so this job cannot be repeated.
This job was printed before PocketPrint kept enough to repeat it.
The copy of %1$s has been cleared from the cache, so it has to be chosen again.
%1$s takes the document as it is, so there is nothing here that the document itself does not already show. Preview is for printers that reduce a page to one bit per dot.
The page could not be rendered.
PocketPrint prints one document at a time; using the first of %1$d shared files.
PocketPrint accepts shared files, not raw file paths.
That file could not be read: %1$s
%1$s is over the %2$d MB limit for a print job.
%1$s took too long to read; nothing was printed.
That text is very long; printing the first %1$d characters.
